raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 45 years, since I was 19 years old. Never went to school — I can't read the words on the fertilizer bags, but I know this soil better than any book. My family has seven mouths to feed. Two of my sons work in Shijiazhuang and send some money home, but I don't like asking them for farm money. This is my responsibility.

I have 8.5 mu total. I split it into two pieces: 5.5 mu on the north side I do wheat then corn, and 3 mu on the south side I plant cotton. I never put everything into one crop. If the bollworm destroys the cotton, I still have grain. If corn prices crash, the cotton saves us.

**Winter wheat** — the wheat is already in the ground from last October. I planted about 35 jin of seed per mu, the same *Lumai* variety my neighbor Lao Wang uses. I bought it from the county supply store for about 25 yuan per mu. Before planting I ran the rotary tiller and spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 50 jin per mu, worked into the soil. Now it's early spring, and I'm watching the color every day. If the wheat turns yellow at jointing, I'll topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. Last year I tried to save money and skipped the topdressing — the yield dropped by more than 100 jin per mu, and I regretted it all winter. I'll irrigate three times: once when it greens up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well is mine, but the electricity for the pump costs money every time — about 30 yuan for the whole field each go. My wife and I do all the work ourselves. My daughter-in-law helps when the factory gives her days off.

**Summer corn** — After wheat harvest in early June, I have two, maybe three days before I must get the corn in the ground. There's no time for deep plowing. I either plant no-till or give it one quick pass with the rotary tiller if the ground is too hard and dry. I use hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu, costs about 45 yuan per mu. I buy it from the same shop every year — last time I bought cheap seed from the market and the ears were half empty. All the fertilizer goes down at planting: compound fertilizer in the seed furrow, one bag per mu. The summer season is too short to split it. I irrigate twice — once right after planting if the weather is dry, and once at the big flare stage. The summer rains usually help, so I don't push it. One spray of herbicide, and I watch for corn borer. If I see holes in the leaves, I spray insecticide quickly.

**Cotton** — I plant cotton in late April on the 3 mu south field. I rotary-till first. Cotton seed is cheaper, about 20 yuan per mu. I put down compound fertilizer before planting — about 40 jin per mu. Cotton doesn't need as much water as wheat, but the drought in May can hurt the seedlings. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if it's very dry in July. The real problem is insects. The bollworm and aphids never stop coming. I spray every 10 days or so from June to August — maybe 12 times in total. Each spray costs about 15 yuan, so that's nearly 200 yuan just for cotton medicine. But if I skip even two sprays, the whole crop is ruined. I pick by hand with family labor. My wife and I pick in rounds from September to October as the bolls open. It's backbreaking work, but hired pickers want 200 yuan a day now, and I can't afford that.

All together, I'll spend about 1,650 yuan on inputs this year. That's a lot of money for me. I have to think carefully about every bag. But if the weather is decent, the wheat should give me about 450 kg per mu, the corn about 500 kg per mu, and the cotton about 500 kg per mu of seed cotton. We'll eat some grain and sell the rest. The cotton all goes to the buyer in the county town. I just hope the prices don't drop like they did three years ago.
